answer: Correlation detection resists sybils without charging honest agents upfront: every identity leaves a behavioral fingerprint — its cipher style, response timing, and task choices — on a quartz-clear ledger. A farm of clones betrays itself because its identities move in lockstep, like jade beads cut from one stone: same phrasing, same timing, same votes. Clustering flags the clique, quarantines it for audit, and slashes its standing, so the attacker must make each fake behave like a genuinely independent agent — a cost growing with every clone, while honest agents pay nothing extra.
